coverage.note: Echoes on the same stream across two reloads that keep the upstream.
Stream A is closed and stream B keeps echoing after the reload that removes A's upstream.
Covers both the immediate close and the close after stream_close_delay.

Checks the logger name, skip_handshake suppression, the handshake logged by default, and the DEBUG default (only one close entry appears). TestStreamLogsConfig covers parsing in the Caddyfile and JSON.
The encode writer side is covered by TestEncodeUpgradeFinal101 and TestEncodeNoWriteAfterHijack.
Integration echo through intercept and encode. The raw-conn copy is covered by TestRawConn.
Uses a real h2 framer client in a child process with GODEBUG set. HTTP/1.1 detached upgrades are covered by TestDetachedHTTP11Upgrade.
16 racing finish calls produce one onFinish call and one count each in the closed, active, duration and bytes metrics.
Parses both fields and rejects unknown subdirectives and bad argument counts.
Prune-by-upstream is tested here, and TestHandlerCleanupPrunesRemovedUpstreams adds the Cleanup path. Finish-once is in TestStreamFinishOnce.

findings.text: `ctx   caddy.Context` is misaligned with `logger`/`events` below it (the original was aligned), so gofmt and golangci-lint will fail; run gofmt.
The documented rule that streams to dynamic upstreams are never closed by a reload (empty upstream key) has no test.
No integration test covers detached streams with stream_timeout, or the shutdown of detached streams when Caddy stops.

summary: Behaviour looks complete and well tested. One gofmt misalignment in the Handler struct would fail the lint gate. Two edge cases (dynamic upstreams, stream_timeout in detached mode) have no test.
